metadata.subject: Physics
metadata.topic: Nuclear Physics — Radioactive Emissions: Name, Range, Stopped By
metadata.note: 3m: complete table — identify emission type, fill in range (alpha), fill in 'stopped by' (gamma + beta). 6 cells total but 3 given (nature). Marks: 0.5m per missing cell × 6 = 3m. Row 1=Gamma (EM, km range, lead/concrete). Row 2=Alpha (helium, short range given as 'few cm'→student fills). Row 3=Beta (electron, few metres, aluminium).

question.name: CSEC Phy Jan 2023 Q6a — Radioactive Emissions Table
question.text:

question.general_feedback:
Radioactive emissions table:

EmissionNatureRange in AirStopped By
Gamma (γ)Electromagnetic radiationSeveral kilometresThick lead or concrete
Alpha (α)Helium nucleus (²⁴He)A few centimetres1 sheet of paper
Beta (β)ElectronA few metresThin aluminium sheet (3 mm Al)

Penetrating power: γ > β > α | Ionising power: α > β > γ

steps.label:
Three types of nuclear radiation: Alpha (α), Beta (β), Gamma (γ)
Key properties: Range in air | What material stops each type
Row 1 — Emission type and what stops it (nature: electromagnetic radiation, range: several km). (1 mark)
Row 2 — Emission type and range in air (nature: helium nucleus, stopped by: paper). (1 mark)
Row 3 — Emission type and what stops it (nature: electron, range: few metres). (1 mark)

fields.label: Emission name (Row 1 — nature: electromagnetic radiation) = _____
fields.diagnostic_hint: Electromagnetic radiation emitted from a nucleus is gamma (γ) radiation

error_codes.SC_METHOD_ERROR: The radiation described as 'electromagnetic radiation' with a very long range is gamma (γ) radiation — not alpha or beta.

fields.label: Gamma radiation is stopped by = _____
fields.diagnostic_hint: Gamma rays require thick lead (or concrete) to stop them due to their high penetrating power

error_codes.SC_METHOD_ERROR: Gamma rays have the highest penetrating power. They require thick lead (several cm) or thick concrete to be effectively stopped.

fields.label: Emission name (Row 2 — nature: helium nucleus, stopped by: paper) = _____
fields.diagnostic_hint: A helium nucleus (⁴₂He) emitted from a radioactive nucleus is an alpha (α) particle

error_codes.SC_METHOD_ERROR: A particle described as a 'helium nucleus' is an alpha (α) particle. It consists of 2 protons and 2 neutrons.

fields.label: Range of alpha particles in air = _____
fields.diagnostic_hint: Alpha particles have a very short range in air — typically 5–8 cm (a few centimetres)

error_codes.SC_METHOD_ERROR: Alpha particles are heavily ionising but have a very short range in air — approximately 5–8 cm (a few centimetres), not metres or kilometres.

fields.label: Emission name (Row 3 — nature: electron, range: few metres) = _____
fields.diagnostic_hint: An electron emitted from a nucleus is a beta (β) particle

error_codes.SC_METHOD_ERROR: An electron emitted from a nucleus is a beta (β) particle — produced when a neutron converts to a proton in the nucleus.

fields.label: Beta particles are stopped by = _____
fields.diagnostic_hint: Beta particles are stopped by a thin sheet of aluminium (approximately 3 mm thick)

error_codes.SC_METHOD_ERROR: Beta particles are stopped by a thin sheet of aluminium (about 3 mm). Paper stops alpha particles but not beta. Lead stops gamma but is overkill for beta.
